name: Multicentric Reticulohistiocytosis with Arthritis

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic papulonodular skin lesions with a coral bead appearance
Severe, symmetric, erosive polyarthritis predominantly affecting distal interphalangeal joints
Skin or synovial biopsy showing multinucleated giant cells and histiocytes with ground-glass eosinophilic cytoplasm
Radiographic evidence of joint erosions and joint space narrowing
Negative rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of papulonodular skin lesions, erosive polyarthritis, and confirmatory histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other histiocytic and rheumatologic disorders.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Papulonodular cutaneous lesions with coral bead appearance
searchTerms: skin bumps with coral bead appearance
papules and nodules resembling coral beads
raised skin lesions with beaded look
severe joint inflammation affecting many joints

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multinucleated giant cells on skin or synovial biopsy
searchTerms: large multinucleated cells in skin or joint biopsy
giant cells seen in tissue samples

common.symptomName: Nail changes including ridging and dystrophy
searchTerms: nail ridges and abnormal nail growth
changes in nail texture and shape
lumps under skin over elbows or knees
subcutaneous nodules on joint extensor surfaces
skin nodules on outer joint areas

occasional.notes: May be present in some cases

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary involvement with interstitial lung disease
searchTerms: lung tissue involvement causing breathing issues

laboratory: Negative rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies
imaging: X-rays showing symmetric joint erosions and joint space narrowing, especially in distal interphalangeal joints
MRI may show synovial inflammation and erosions
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations identified
other: Skin or synovial biopsy demonstrating multinucleated giant cells with ground-glass eosinophilic cytoplasm

distinguishingFeatures: Positive rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies
Predominantly affects proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints
Absence of characteristic papulonodular skin lesions
Localized skin nodules without systemic arthritis
Histopathology lacking multinucleated giant cells typical of MRH
Presence of ANA and other autoantibodies
Multisystem involvement with characteristic malar rash

redFlags: Rapidly progressive erosive arthritis leading to joint destruction
Development of systemic symptoms such as unexplained fever and weight loss
Presence of pulmonary or ocular involvement indicating systemic spread
references: Miettinen M, Fetsch JF. Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis: a clinicopathologic and immunohistochemical study of 42 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 1991.
Wang J, et al. Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis: clinical features and treatment outcomes. Clin Rheumatol. 2019.
